cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Philippi, and he's in chains while he writes it (Phil 1:13). He's near the end of his letter, and now he gets to the thank-you part. He says he rejoices greatly in the Lord that at last they've revived their concern for him.

cards.question: Paul says the Philippians cared about him all along. So why hadn't they shown it?

answers.text: They had no opportunity to show it
They didn't know where he was staying
They were waiting for him to ask them

cards.text: Then Paul jumps in quick: he's not saying this out of need. Not like me when a baker brings me cookies, going "Oh, you didn't have to!" while my mustache is ALREADY halfway in the box.

cards.question: Paul says, "I have learned to be ___ regardless of my circumstances."
Paul says the secret he's learned, in any and every situation, is how to always have plenty.

cards.text: Filled or hungry, plenty or need, Paul has learned to handle both. And then he says the line people put on everything from T-shirts to gym walls.

cards.question: Paul says he can do all things. Through whom?

answers.text: Through Christ who gives him strength
Through the friends who support him

cards.question: Paul doesn't want the Philippians thinking their gift didn't matter. He says, "Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my ___."

cards.text: Then Paul takes them back to the early days of the gospel, when he left Macedonia. You know that group chat where everybody says "we got you," and then ONE person actually shows up?

cards.question: When Paul left Macedonia, how many churches besides the Philippians partnered with him in giving and receiving?
While Paul was in Thessalonica, the Philippians provided for his needs only once.
Paul says he's not seeking a gift. He's looking for the ___ that may be credited to the Philippians' account.

cards.text: Their gifts reached Paul by Epaphroditus, the messenger the Philippians sent to take care of his needs (Phil 2:25). Special delivery to a man in chains, no tracking number, just faith and a good pair of sandals.

cards.question: After getting the gifts from Epaphroditus, Paul says he has all he needs and more.
Paul says the Philippians' gifts are well-pleasing to God. What does he call them?

cards.text: Now Paul tells them his God will supply all of their needs. Friend, that thank-you note beats any cookie I have EVER stamped, and I have stamped some GOOD ones.

cards.question: Paul says God will supply all the Philippians' needs. According to what?

answers.text: His glorious riches in Christ Jesus
How much they have given to Paul

cards.text: Paul bursts into praise: "To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen." Then he tells them, "Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus."

cards.question: The brothers with Paul send greetings, and so do all the saints. Which saints does Paul point out especially?

answers.text: Those from the church in Jerusalem
Those from the city of Ephesus

cards.text: Saints in the household of Caesar, the Roman emperor himself, sending greetings all the way to Philippi! Then Paul signs off: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "I have learned to be ___ regardless of my circumstances.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time on this card, but the card never says who he is. It only says he is writing to the church in Philippi and is in chains. He needs a simple introduction, such as Paul the apostle.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question begins "Paul doesn't want the Philippians thinking their gift didn't matter." That gives a motive for why Paul says verse 14, and the text never states it. Verse 14 only says "Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction."

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The group chat joke, where everybody says "we got you" and ONE person shows up, gives away the answer to card 10 (no other church partnered with Paul). It can also push the baker toward the wrong answer "Only one." The joke also suggests that other churches promised help, which the text never says (Phil 4:15).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess Paul's exact wording ("fruit" against "praise" and "honor"). No story card sets up the idea of something credited to the Philippians' account, so the baker can't reason out "fruit" over the other two words. This is a guess at the words of the line, not at its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: "A freewill vow" is not a real detail from the Bible. Scripture speaks of a vow or a freewill offering, not a freewill vow. It also sits close to the right answer, since the Philippians' gift was given freely, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
